description: Report or act on the device keyboard. The status action reports whether the keyboard is visible and, when it is, what its return key offers: `returnKey` is go, search, send, next, done, previous, join, route, continue, enter, none, or unknown, and `returnKeyLabel` is the wording that return key itself shows when the platform can read it, trimmed of surrounding whitespace, which can be an app's custom or a localized string. A label appears only for a key the platform identified as the return key. `none` means the field offers no action key, which only Android can establish; `unknown` means this read could not name the key, not that the keyboard has one: on iOS the identified key carries wording this read does not map, or the keyboard exposes no return key it can identify at all — a number, decimal or phone pad has none, and then no label is reported either; on Android the editor's imeOptions name no action. A hidden keyboard reports neither field. The get action answers the same as status. The dismiss action hides the keyboard. It taps the keyboard dismiss/hide key when one is exposed, verifies the keyboard closed, and reports UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION when the keyboard stays up — background taps are never attempted. On iOS a keyboard with no dismiss key adds error.details.reason keyboard_dismiss_unavailable with dispatched: no; one whose key was tapped and stayed visible has no reason and dispatched: unknown. Android reports keyboard_dismiss_unavailable with dispatched: unknown, since its own dismiss keyevents were already sent. The enter action presses the return key. Times out after 90s.

device.description: Device name; ids go in udid or serial.
